question.text: How many federal units will Fiocruz's InfoGripe SE 44 bulletin (released 12 November 2026) flag with SRAG incidence at alert level or above and a rising long-term trend?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves using the "Resumo do Boletim InfoGripe – Semana Epidemiológica (SE) 44 2026" published by Fiocruz, expected at https://agencia.fiocruz.br/sites/agencia.fiocruz.br/files/Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_44.pdf ; a version of that file with a filename suffix (e.g. Resumo_InfoGripe_2026_44_0.pdf) counts as the same document. The resolved value is the number of Brazilian federal units (26 states plus the Federal District, out of 27 total) that this edition reports as having SRAG incidence at alert level, risk level, or high risk (based on the last two weeks) together with a rising long-term trend (last six weeks) — the figure given in the edition's national-situation bullet of the form "N das 27 unidades federativas apresentam incidência de SRAG em nível de alerta ou risco (últimas duas semanas) com sinal de crescimento na tendência de longo prazo (últimas 6 semanas) até a semana 44", followed by the names of those units. If the edition lists the qualifying units without stating a total, count the distinct units listed; if a stated total and the number of units named disagree, the stated total prevails. If the SE 44 summary is not hosted at that URL or a suffixed variant, the same document published elsewhere on agencia.fiocruz.br or fiocruz.br, or Fiocruz's own press release reporting the SE 44 figure, may be used; failing that, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) may be used. If publication of the SE 44 edition is delayed beyond 13 November 2026, the question resolves on that edition once it is published.
question.fine_print: A "federal unit" (unidade federativa, UF) means one of Brazil's 26 states or the Federal District. A UF counts as "at alert level or above" if the bulletin classifies its SRAG incidence over the last two weeks as "nível de alerta", "nível de risco", or "alto risco" (any level above the low/green baseline). If Fiocruz publishes a corrected version of the SE 44 summary before 23:59 UTC on 13 November 2026, the corrected version is used.

## 1. Resolution source

- I found no CSV, JSON or dashboard file that gives the per-state alert-level and trend classification ahead of the bulletin.

## 2. Current status

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-29 (SE 42): No news coverage turned up in my searches. Searching on the state names returned nothing for 29 October.
- 2026-10-15 (SE 40, data from 4 to 10 October): Afya reported 1 state (Sergipe) with alert-level incidence and growth, mainly in children under 2, linked to metapneumovirus. Metapneumovirus was rising in SP, RJ, ES, MS, PR, AL, BA, PE and SE, but only Sergipe combined that with alert level. MA, MT, MS, RS, RR and SC were at alert, risk or high risk without growth. Fiocruz described the national picture as stable or oscillating. [source](https://portal.afya.com.br/infectologia/srag-no-brasil-mantem-estabilidade-mas-sergipe-segue-em-alerta)
- 2026-10-08 (SE 39): Brasil 61 reported 3 states (AL, RR, SE), with the rise mostly among children and adolescents. This came from the search summary; I did not open the article. [source](https://brasil61.com/14-10-2026-04-25h)
- 2026-08-22 (SE 32): 2 states (BA, SE). Rondônia and Piauí showed slight growth but were not at alert level. [source](https://brasil61.com/n/infogripe-casos-de-srag-seguem-em-queda-no-pais-bras2616981.amp)

## 4. Base rates
Figures for 2026 so far:
- SE 32: 2
- SE 39: 3
- SE 40: 1
- SE 41: 3 (from the background only)
- SE 42: 5 (from the background only)

From SE 39 to SE 42 the count moved by 2 states each week, sometimes up, sometimes down. Sergipe has been on the list every week since at least SE 39.

The same period in 2025:
- 2025-10-09, SE 40: 7 states (AM, GO, PR, PA, RJ, RR, SC). [source](https://agenciagov.ebc.com.br/noticias/202510/infogripe-casos-de-influenza-a-avancam-para-sao-paulo)
- 2025-10-30, SE 43: 6 states (AC, ES, MS, RJ, SC, TO). The article says "tendência de crescimento" without saying long-term. [source](https://brasil61.com/n/casos-de-srag-por-influenza-avancam-para-o-rio-de-janeiro-e-espirito-santo-bras2515050)
- 2025-11-06, SE 44: 3 states (MS, PB, TO). This is the same week as the target, one year earlier. [source](https://brasil61.com/n/casos-de-sindrome-respiratoria-grave-avancam-no-sudeste-e-ligam-alerta-em-novos-estados-bras2515113)
- 2025-11-13, SE 45: 3 states (MS, PA, RJ), mostly driven by rhinovirus. Another 11 states were at alert level or above without growth. [source](https://brasil61.com/n/infogripe-alerta-aumento-de-srag-entre-criancas-em-ms-pa-e-rj-bras2515148)

What this suggests:
- At this point in the season the count has stayed between 1 and 7 in both years.
- From one week to the next it usually moves by 0 to 3, and it fell by 3 between SE 43 and SE 44 in 2025.
- A state can move between "alert without growth" and "alert with growth" (and back) in a single week, so the pool of states currently at alert without growth matters. At SE 42 that was RR and SC.

## 5. Other forecasts
- No prediction market or expert forecast exists on this question or anything close to it. None of the Kalshi or Polymarket markets in the supplied list matches it; they cover Brazilian inflation, elections and similar topics.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution

- Things to watch:

  - The rising three-week national trend reported at SE 42.
  - Whether RR and SC pick up a growth signal.

(a) **Time left:** About 10 days. The SE 44 bulletin is expected on 12 November 2026. Before that, the SE 43 edition comes out on 5 November, so this forecast is two weekly steps ahead of the latest data.

(b) **Latest known value:** SE 42, published 29 October 2026, showed 5 UFs: AP, MA, MT, MS and SE. RR and SC were at alert level without growth.

(c) **If nothing changed:** 5.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** The weekly sequence has run 3, 1, 3, 5. The national three-week trend was rising and metapneumovirus is spreading, which points to 5 to 7. However, early November is usually a low-activity period. In 2025 the count fell from 6 at SE 43 to 3 at SE 44, so mean reversion toward about 3 to 4 is also plausible.

(e) **Historical variation:** Week-to-week changes are usually 0 to 3 UFs. Over two weeks the swing can be up to about 4. In both 2025 and 2026, values in this part of the season ranged from 1 to 7.

(f) **Experts and markets:** There are no markets or published forecasts on this. Fiocruz described the national picture as oscillation with a short-term increase.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** Reporting backlogs flatten the six-week trends and the metapneumovirus and rhinovirus waves in children peak. Sergipe then drops out or the list falls to 0 or 1 UFs.
- **High:** Metapneumovirus and rhinovirus spread across the Centre-South and Northeast, or there is an early influenza or COVID uptick. Several UFs currently at alert without growth (RR, SC, RS) gain growth signals at the same time as new states such as SP, PR, BA and PE join, pushing the count to 10 or more.
